name: wordpress
description: Recognises WordPress sites and records what they give away about themselves — the core version, the plugins and themes installed, the REST namespaces plugins register and the user accounts exposed — as findings. It reads the Map, not the traffic, and is passive by default. Turn on active version scanning and it will also request the readme.txt / style.css of a plugin or theme whose version the traffic never stated, the way wpscan pins a version down.

settings.label: Read the responses the Map was built from
settings.description: On: the plugin reads the page an endpoint was discovered in, and the responses served from it, for versions and REST data. Off: only the endpoints' own paths are read.

settings.label: Record the user accounts a site exposes
settings.description: Author archives, the REST users route and oEmbed replies name accounts without being asked.

settings.label: Record REST API namespaces
settings.description: A namespace core doesn't register is a plugin's footprint, even when that plugin serves no assets.

settings.label: Actively request a plugin's or theme's version
settings.description: Off: the plugin stays passive and reports only what the traffic carried. On: when a plugin or theme is found whose version the traffic never stated, it requests that part's readme.txt (plugins) or style.css (themes) to read the version, the way wpscan does. These requests go to the site, so this is active testing; they are kept to the hosts your targets cover and shown in the Traffic list.
